h1: Provider Connector Shared API Sequences and Reuse Assessment
p: Summary · Logical contract · Sequences and reuse
The diagrams use the established onboarding responsibility labels and UML sequence style. Blue marks proposed handoffs; activation bars show handling, not elapsed time.
The shared-contract direction is confirmed by CA-ARCH01/02 in 044 REF. Sequence calls below are logical until mapped to actual API versions; notifications are not a second invoice API.
The sequences implement 045 CA-01–05. They show logical boundaries; protocol and deployment remain architecture decisions.

A validates the product request at the shared API. B dispatches saved work through notifications to one executor; the Provider Connector calls the external platform and posts the correlated result to that same API. C holds uncertain effects, reconciles the original operation when permitted and submits recovered evidence through the shared API. A provider acting directly uses the same contract under its assigned role; it must not execute work already assigned to a connector.

A shows polling and qualified push as alternative entry paths. B submits source data through the shared API and confirms durable capture before covered progress advances. C retries that same submission after interruption; shared-API duplicate handling prevents repeated business processing. A product retrieves permitted saved content through that same API. Expired cursors or source gaps require qualified recovery before a completeness claim. No SPFE push interface is established by the reviewed baseline.

045 §4 holds CS01–16, including changes during pending work, partial outcomes and country/profile isolation. Those cases refer to the applicable diagram branch or the owning feature rather than adding one diagram per exception.

Preferred transformation implementation candidate upstream
DTS + invoice-feature owners: qualify exact build, input/output mappings, rule packs and operations. No transformation responsibility moves into provider connector transport.
Spain identity, routing, public-copy and reporting rules
Spain-specific feature rules, referenced rather than copied
Country/domain owners: bind approved rules; prove another country's profile does not inherit Spain behaviour.
Future peer interconnection
Shared design candidate; implementation reuse unknown
Operator/Architecture owners: qualify peer protocol, trust, role and capability differences. No automatic reuse of customer-provider credentials or adapters.

p: These gates refine existing SPEC013 GPA-Q01–12 and SPEC014 decisions; they do not create a second approval process.

tr.td: Interface direction and ownership / API Architecture

Use the confirmed common contract for product, provider and connector consumers. Map historical labels and exact operation versions; qualify notification/callback interfaces separately. Select one executor and reconciler per mutation.
Private scope / Product + Provider Integration

Use the six-provider portfolio in PRD214, including Sovos. Confirm selected Spain services and direct versus aggregated access. Complete the 045 matrix with contract version, environment, owner and source evidence for each binding.
Contract and trust / API Architecture + Security

Define actual request/result schemas, authentication, authorised destinations, credential custody/rotation, callback replay protection and compatibility policy. Do not expose arbitrary endpoint execution.
Runtime and operations / Engineering + Operations
Select shared versus isolated deployment from trust and load needs. Set measured timeouts, quotas, payload limits, evidence retention and support ownership; no numeric targets are established here.
Conformance / Integration + domain owners
Execute applicable CS01–16 under CA-01–05, selected external-contract checks and existing-consumer compatibility. Record build/version and results.

p: Historical CA-H01, canonical CA-BASE and original public CA-SPFE sources, versions and limits are recorded in 044 REF. Public operation sources SPFE-S10–S17/S23 are mapped in 045 REF. These sequences and gates are proposed design controls, not AEAT-prescribed components.

Reuse sources: SPEC017, Part 1 §§2–4 and REF, establishes the proposed provider binding and its contract gaps; SPEC008, Spain use/reuse and qualification gates, establishes the DTS assessment boundary. Neither proves a deployed Spain implementation. Public source selection remains the reviewed manifest, current_wsdl_baseline, and the 23 November release review.
